_what: RUBY_DECLARATION_SPEC proposal for script/m14/project-index.ts (Lead applies; lane does not edit Lead-owned files). Charter-first deliverable of the ruby index scoping phase. Every field is derived from the pinned tree-sitter-ruby grammar's named nodes and the ruby analyzer's existing per-file rules; nothing here invents a construct.
status: PROPOSAL — analyzer-side consumption must stay behind a flag and fail-closed; no analyzer change until Lead approves the patch

typeNodes.when: LHS constant, RHS call on Class/Struct/Data/Module (`K = Class.new(Base)`, `Point = Struct.new(:x)`, `Cfg = Data.define(:h)`)
typeNodes.kind: factory-declared Class/Module, carries base relation when RHS is Class.new(constant)

typeNodes.when: LHS constant, RHS simple constant (`Alias = Other`)
typeNodes.kind: Constant alias — nameOnly, NOT a type declaration

memberNodes.note: `def obj.m` with obj not `self`/constant is UNNAMEABLE and refused (analyzer refuses it today)

memberNodes.spelling: as the alias name, member of the enclosing scope; record aliased target as metadata, never as a separate declaration
property members Owner#x and Owner#x= per accessor kind

memberNodes.when: LHS constant inside a class/module body

baseNodes.field: superclass (the grammar wraps it: superclass -> constant/scope_resolution)
baseNodes.spelling: static constant path only; a call base (`(expr)`, `Struct.new(...)`) is UNNAMEABLE for `extends` and refused

baseNodes.when: include/prepend/extend with a constant/scope_resolution argument at any class/module/body scope
baseNodes.spelling: source = composing type, target = the constant path; role recorded (include|prepend|extend) as metadata.mixinType — RUBY-D1

baseNodes.when: `K = Class.new(Base)` with a static constant base

scopeNodes.kind: type scope; reopens the SAME declaration
type scope; reopens the SAME declaration
singleton scope of the enclosing type — NOT a new type, no own name
binding scope (locals; never a type scope)
binding scope, inherits enclosing type scope

nameOnlyNodes.use: REMOVES X from the exported/constant surface (record as a visibility fact, not a declaration)
member declaration names (see memberNodes); the CALL itself is not a declaration

nestingAndReopening.rule: The nesting stack (class/module/singleton_class, entering methods does NOT open a type scope) builds the qualified path. A declaration occurrence is recorded as a SITE under its qualified path; OCCURRENCES OF THE SAME (kind, qualified path) IN THE SAME PROJECT ARE ONE DECLARATION WITH MULTIPLE SITES (file,line). Ruby reopens classes by design; reading reopens as separate declarations would manufacture false ambiguity — the sizing instrument shows exactly how much false ambiguity a naive multi-site count creates (instantiates 481, extends 986, mixes_in 123 rows are WEAK only because of this).
nestingAndReopening.anonymous: A scope without a static name (bare `Class.new do ... end`, `class << obj`) is UNNAMEABLE: its members are not declared in the project space (the analyzer's namable-owner rule, reused unchanged).
nestingAndReopening.topLevel: A file-scope `def` is a private method of Object; spell it `Object#name` (record also `isTopLevel=true`) so it can never collide with a class-named member.

spellingContract.types: A::B::C — constant path from the nesting stack; the LEAF is also indexed for leaf-name lookup and the FULL path for qualified lookup.
spellingContract.instanceMembers: A::B#m (hash form is mandatory; it is the only thing distinguishing instance from singleton)
spellingContract.membersWrittenAsAccessors: A::B#x (reader), A::B#x= (writer) per attr kind; singleton accessors A::B.x
spellingContract.constants: A::B::CONST; top-level CONST indexed both as CONST and ::CONST
spellingContract.aliases: declared under their NEW name only (the aliased target is metadata; a resolution that binds the alias target to the original spelling would double-count one member)

visibility.record: per member: public|protected|private (+ module_function flag); the declaration SPACE includes private members (they are real declarations); resolution may use visibility for ranking but must never delete a declaration on visibility
visibility.private_constant: removes the constant from the reachable space for exports only; the declaration remains for type/member resolution

indexFactsRequested.symbols: one row per declaration: qualified path(s), kind, sites[], visibility, enclosing type, basePaths[] (superclass/mixins), factory flag
indexFactsRequested.typeExists: set of declared type paths + leaf map (for classic leaf-name lookup)
indexFactsRequested.memberOf: owner path -> member qualified names (both # and . forms)
indexFactsRequested.reopenSafe: multi-site rows are ONE declaration — resolution must never read site count as ambiguity
indexFactsRequested.completeness: the index exposes a completeness flag (all admitted files indexed); consumers FAIL CLOSED when false (no partial resolution, no new edges, metadata unchanged)

analyzerConsumptionSketch.flag: behind a lane flag/env (fail-closed on incomplete index), metadata-only like the cpp pattern: facts are read, no edge is fabricated by the index itself
uses: overrides: verify the first-parent GUESS against the index (base class declared + base declares the method) -> structural confidence instead of a declared cause
instantiates/extends/mixes_in: resolve a static constant path against declared types (reopen-safe) instead of name-only ambiguity
calls: ONLY where the analyzer already carries owner/type evidence (it currently does not for bare calls) — leave name-based rows untouched; no owner inference from the index alone
never: no cross-file method binding for bare calls without owner evidence
no ivar resolution from the index (the @sigil wall is not a declaration-space problem)

preCommittedArmTable.edges: INVARIANT at 85,234 (an index must not add or drop a row)
preCommittedArmTable.predictedMovement: resolved 24,328 -> up to +4,844 (upper bound = residual rows the sizing classified decidable: overrides 3,013 base-verified + instantiates 481 + extends 987 + mixes_in 130 + calls 231 unique-declaration + uses 2); causeOK 2,943 -> falls by the verified overrides guesses; amb(decl) falls by the reopened-declaration rows that become unique; unresolved falls by the rows whose declaration the index supplies
preCommittedArmTable.mustNotMove: TOTAL/edges, extOK/ext?/extFAIL/bind*/causeFAIL (all 0/unchanged), arbitraryTwin must NOT rise (expect fall), closure identity exact
preCommittedArmTable.declined: every row the index could not decide is reported as declined BY REASON (owner-absent, not-declared, reopen-ambiguous, visibility-only, dynamic) and counted — never merged into resolved
preCommittedArmTable.falsifier: if edges move, or arbitraryTwin rises, or any failure column is nonzero, or resolved rises above the decidable upper bound, the consumption is over-reaching and is reverted

fixturesPlan: cross-file-override-verified: subclass in file A, base class+method in file B -> overrides resolved structurally; same fixture with the index absent -> unchanged first-parent cause (fail-closed)

cross-file-instantiation-class: `Foo.new` in file A, `class Foo` in file B -> instantiates resolves; a same-named class in TWO namespaces in the repo stays ambiguous (reopen is not ambiguity, distinct paths are)
reopen-is-one-declaration: `class Foo` split across two files with members in each -> NOT ambiguous, all members resolve
mixin-module-sibling: `include Mod` with `module Mod` in a sibling file -> mixes_in resolves; dynamic `include(local_mod)` still refused
fail-closed: index completeness=false -> every one of the above gives the pre-index result byte-identically (this is a RED-capable control)

secondaryLocalBindingCensus.question: can ruby honestly emit LOCAL-BINDING claims?
secondaryLocalBindingCensus.ruled: YES — the analyzer already carries the evidence: its method-body walker builds a per-method `locals` set (parameters, param defaults, assignment LHS, block params) and suppresses `calls` for bound names. So a bare read is distinguishable from a method call at the analyzer's own evidence tier, exactly the property a binding claim needs.
secondaryLocalBindingCensus.measuredNow: text-level over-approximation: 17,579 residual calls/uses rows whose target spelling also appears as an assignment word somewhere in the row's repo (NOT scope-exact; the repo-wide local set cannot distinguish a same-named local in another method).
secondaryLocalBindingCensus.whatItProves: a scope-exact instrument (analyzer-run, per-method locals) is required before pricing claims; the count above is an UPPER bound and is labelled as such. No claim kind is invented lane-side; if the Lead wants the class claimed, the existing binding claim path is the mechanism.
secondaryLocalBindingCensus.falsifier: a residual bare call whose name is provably a method-scope local in the ROW'S OWN METHOD yet was emitted as a call = a binding gap in the analyzer, reportable row by row.
